spec.name: unreadable-runtime-config
spec.intent: Census @2f2a0238 (design and notebook at 2f2a0238); every path is repo-relative on the plan's line. A line number, count or observed behaviour cited here is a measurement at that commit: re-derive it if its path changed since. Add no new test file: a new one must be classified in packages/canon/test/gate-convicts.test.ts, which no unit of this plan owns; extend the test files named in outputs. Run one test file inside its package with `pnpm exec vitest run <file>` (a `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- <file>` runs the whole suite). Sequenced after isolated-implementer and isolated-landing by the operator's ruling that the note 'implementers edit the main checkout' is realized first. Realize the command line's no-footguns clause, nothing written where the consumer did not ask and every error saying what went wrong and what to do, for a runtime config cratylus cannot read (note 'install replaces an unparseable runtime config unread'). At 2f2a0238 emitRuntimeConfig reads a runtime config that is not valid JSON, or not a JSON object, as empty (priorConfig, packages/forge/src/deploy/runtime-config.ts:344-353, 'A corrupt config must not wedge a deploy'), so install and deploy rewrite the file whole and the host's bytes are lost without a word; uninstall's removeRuntimeStanza (packages/forge/src/cli/commands/uninstall.ts:436-450) leaves such a file unread and says nothing. CHANGE. Install (its dry run included) and deploy, when the runtime config they would write exists and cannot be read as a JSON object, refuse before anything is placed: one line `cratylus install: <file> <what is wrong>; <what to do>` (repair the file or move it away, then run install again), the same shape the command uses for a cratylus.config.ts it cannot load, exit 1, nothing written anywhere; deploy the same in its own name. Uninstall leaves such a file byte for byte and names it among what it left, saying why. A missing file and a readable one behave as today. Every test sets AGENT_RUNTIME_CONFIG to a file of its own, so none reaches the operator's real ~/.cratylus.json (note 'uninstall in a test reaches the real runtime config'). packages/cli/README.md, where it describes the host runtime config, says so. .changeset/unreadable-runtime-config.md: patch for @cratylus/forge and cratylus.
accept: in packages/forge, with the packages its tests need built, `pnpm exec vitest run test/cli/install.test.ts` exits 0, including a case: AGENT_RUNTIME_CONFIG names a file holding `not json`; install exits 1, prints one stderr line naming that file and what to do, leaves the file's bytes unchanged and places nothing under the target home; the same with a file holding `[1]`; at 2f2a0238 the case fails (the file is rewritten)

in packages/forge, `pnpm exec vitest run test/deploy/uninstall.test.ts` exits 0, including a case where uninstall meets a runtime config holding `not json`: the file is left byte for byte and the report names it as left; at 2f2a0238 the report does not name it

missing: command line: every error says what to do — the uninstall line naming an unreadable runtime config tells the operator to repair it and run `cratylus uninstall --harness <h>` again, but that same uninstall has already removed the deploy record, so the rerun reports 'no deploy record … nothing is removed' and the harness's stanza stays in the repaired file; the remedy it gives does not work (the packages/cli README repeats it as 'then run the command again')
